article.story:
Dominik Szoboszlai converted a stoppage-time penalty to snatch a draw as Newcastle and Liverpool served up a Premier League thriller of which Kevin Keegan would have been proud.

The Hungary international struck in the ninth minute of added time to clinch a 2-2 draw which extended his side's unbeaten run at St James' Park to 10 games after Lewis Hall had been adjudged to have brought down substitute Víctor Muñoz.

It was tough on the hosts, who looked to have won it through substitute Joe Willock's 57th-minute strike just seconds after his introduction in the wake of the Cody Gakpo equaliser which had cancelled out Anthony Elanga's first-half opener.

On a day when Tyneside and Merseyside united to celebrate Keegan's contribution to both clubs, Yoane Wissa turned in his best performance yet for Newcastle as £130million man Alexander Isak, the man he was in part bought to replace, suffered a miserable return to St James' in front of a hostile crowd of 52,630.

New Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, who has had just weeks to work with a squad which could still be reshaped further before the transfer window closes, will have been delighted with much of what he saw from his players, while opposite number Andoni Iraola headed back across the Pennines relieved, but with questions to be answered.

Both sets of players had emerged for the warm-up wearing Keegan number seven shirts before an emotional tribute, but the temperature rose significantly on kick-off with Isak a target for the home fans.

The jeers turned to rapturous cheers after just five minutes when impressive debutant Amar Dedic slid the ball into the path of Will Osula, who timed his pass to Elanga to perfection and looked on as the Sweden international raced away from Milos Kerkez before slotting a right-foot shot across Alisson Becker and into the far corner.

The visitors' response was immediate and goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek reacted well to make a fine save from Florian Wirtz's deflected 18th-minute attempt, but with Jaissle's men careless in possession, they repeatedly invited pressure they did not need.

Lewis Miley's raking 22nd-minute pass allowed Dedic to fire in a shot which clipped Kerkez and looped out for a corner and Jérémy Jacquet did just enough to prevent Osula from latching on to Wissa's through-ball.

For all they continued to dominate possession, Liverpool were creating little of note, Szoboszlai drilling a 26th-minute free-kick straight into the defensive wall after being tugged back by Wissa, and the half-time whistle arrived with the home side's narrow lead intact.

Szoboszlai caused problems with an early corner as the game resumed, but the Magpies might have done better after Harvey Barnes and Elanga broke at pace, but failed to punish the Reds, and Miley was similarly unable to test Alisson with a 48th-minute effort.

Cody Gakpo curled a 53rd-minute strike just over with Hornicek rooted to the spot, but he was much more accurate two minutes later when he was given time and space to rifle the ball past the keeper with a skidding 25-yard drive.

However, Newcastle were quickly back in front after Wissa's quick feet opened up space for substitute Willock, who stepped inside before shooting unerringly across Alisson.

Jaissle's side threatened to add to their tally with substitute Jacob Ramsey dragging a 70th-minute volley wide and Alisson denying Wissa one-on-one.

But they were undone at the death when referee Stuart Attwell, to Hall's anguish and surprise, pointed to the spot and Szoboszlai obliged from 12 yards.

article.story:
Alexander Isak marked his return from injury with the winner as Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford 2-1.

The Reds were misfiring as they trailed to Keane Lewis-Potter's first-half goal, but the match turned on a needless red card for Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk on the stroke of half-time.

Víctor Muñoz hauled Liverpool level after the break before Isak struck with his fifth goal of the season.

Brentford then lost Vitaly Janelt to second yellow card in stoppage time.

Swedish striker Isak had missed the previous two matches but was able start alongside Florian Wirtz and recent signing Bradley Barcola in a £350 million frontline.

Barcola, who hit a hat-trick against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday, should have opened his Premier League account after Janelt's mistake left him with a free run on goal.

The £123m wideman attempted to chip onrushing Bees keeper Caoimhín Kelleher but made an almighty mess of his effort, tamely stabbing the ball wide to prompt a chorus of "what a waste of money" from the home fans behind the goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury lasted just 32 minutes before the Reds midfielder was forced off with what appeared to be a recurrence of his knee problem.

Liverpool were awarded a penalty after Dango Ouattara looked for all the world like he had tripped Alexis Mac Allister in the area.

However, a VAR review showed the Bees attacker had got the slightest touch on the ball, and after a check on the monitor referee John Brooks overturned his decision.

Two minutes later Brentford took the lead when Lewis-Potter, among the smallest players on the pitch, met Igor Thiago's cross with a bullet header into the top corner.

But in stoppage time Brentford fell foul of a VAR decision, when Yarmoliuk was spotted to have aimed a 'headbutting action' towards Jérémy Jacquet as the pair grappled at a corner.

The Ukrainian's red mist earned him a red card, although Liverpool were not awarded a penalty as the ball was not in play.

Nevertheless, Liverpool made the most of their numerical advantage in the second half.

They equalised when Wirtz sent Muñoz racing down the right and the Spanish winger turned inside Lewis-Potter before arrowing a left-foot shot past Kelleher.

The winner arrived in the 70th minute when Mac Allister swung a deep cross towards the far post, Barcola headed the ball back and Isak took a touch before lashing it past Kelleher.

To rub salt in the Brentford wounds, German midfielder Janelt was sent off in stoppage time for pulling back Rio Ngumoha.

article.story:
Uncertainty may surround Manchester City's future but nothing changed for them on the pitch as the Premier League leaders successfully came through their first public examination since being found guilty on breaches of the league's financial rules by an independent commission.

Having been subjected to a febrile atmosphere at Anfield where they were labelled cheats and booed at every opportunity Enzo Maresca's side shrugged off the slurs relating to the numerous breaches of financial rules to win 3-0.

The way they brushed off the taunts was similar to the way the club, who have lodged an appeal, have treated the decision of the independent commission and the fact it was business as usual showed there appears to be no visible concerns from the players when it comes to delivering on the pitch.

Erling Haaland made the crucial breakthrough in front of his father Alfe-Inge -- stood with the away fans waving their throwback inflatable yellow bananas --  just three minutes after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second bookable offence, both soft yellow cards.

Subsitute Jérémy Doku, who helped turn the game the visitors' way after coming on in the 56th minute, curled home a second and Rayan Cherki rolled in a third to allow Maresca the luxury of resting Haaland with 10 minutes remaining with their first back-to-back league wins at Anfield since January 1953 safely secured.

Liverpool fans have reason more than most to feel aggrieved at City's sham contracts which allowed them to inject £830 million of inflated income over nine seasons, having been beaten to the title three times by their north-west rivals.

The resumption of the Premier League allowed them first go at venting their fury but they will not be the last.

But abuse from the stands will not derail this team, who have no association with that period. That will come in the form of a Premier League punishment should their appeal fail.

City would not have relished the trip to a ground where their record is the worst but their opponents were weakened by the absence of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, and dealt another blow when Dominik Szoboszlai was ruled out with a hamstring problem.

There was not a great deal of football played in the first half but a huge amount of energy expended as the home side's high tempo pressed the life out of City with Lewis Koumas, on his full Premier League debut, and Víctor Muñoz particularly effective.

Marc Guéhi had a testing time against both and when Rúben Dias hauled Koumas to the ground a scuffle ensured between Alexis Mac Allister and Elliot Anderson.

Liverpool's dominance of the first half - City did not have a shot until the 35th minute - began to evaporate after the break after Koumas and Gravenberch had shots parried by Gianluigi Donnarumma and Mac Allister fired wide in the space of a minute.

A dangerous Antoine Semenyo cross was cleared by Milos Kerkez before Haaland's first sight of goal, with only Alisson Becker to beat, saw the striker roll his shot wide.

But the dismissal of Gravenberch after clumsily catching the heels of Doku proved pivotal. While Liverpool waited to send on a like-for-like replacement in Trey Nyoni, one swing of Haaland's left foot effectively decided the contest.

Doku and Cherki ensured Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola's first defeat was a painful one.
